doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

chapter: Songs, singers and the state of jazz
title: Early blues singers as influences
summary: Bessie Smith did not influence her; she heard those singers only later.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: That pretty much answers my question about the blues. The early blues singers — Bessie Smith — did they have any influence on your singing style?
No. My influences came from, I didn’t hear them at all until later on in the years. Because they started like talking about them. I don’t know exactly what year, but no. I had never
heard Bessie Smith or her sister Mamie Smith. The only one that I remember is “L’il Green.” [sings] In the dark it’s just you and I. You remember that?

You’re too young. I tell my friend that. He’s a drummer and he works with me sometimes. And I say, “Do you remember this, Joe?” And he’ll say, “Etta, I was in my playpen then.” So I say, “God will get you for this.”
